title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets), i.e. the relations defining the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group, with ρ of order 3 and σ of order 2 the standard torsion generators of (the profinite completion of) SL(2,Z). On the preceding pages he builds a group of 'relations' M_{ρ,σ} = SM_{ρ,σ}/L_0. Its elements are triples (α,β,f), equivalently data (u, a, b, U) with a ∈ T_ρ, b ∈ N'_σ, U ∈ G. The maps between the two descriptions are α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, f = u U^{-1} (formula (40)). Here T_ρ and N'_σ are torus/normaliser-type groups attached to ρ and σ, and δ_ρ, δ_σ, δ_G are 'determinant'/cyclotomic-type characters. The proposition of p.540/536' says the image of SM_{ρ,σ} → B'_0 × T_ρ × T'_σ × G is cut out by det u = det b = det U =: μ and det a/μ ∈ μ_n.

This page, §10: two distinguished 'sub-group-relations'.

(1) M_{ρ,σ}(σ) is defined by β_0 = 1, i.e. β = f. By (40) this means U = b. Given any (a,b) in τ_{ρ,σ}, that is with δ_ρ(a)/δ_σ(b) ∈ μ_n, the simplest lift to M_{ρ,σ} is U := b. The determinant condition then holds automatically, since δ_G(U) = δ_σ(b). So M_{ρ,σ}(σ) is a section of M_{ρ,σ} → τ_{ρ,σ}.

(2) M_{ρ,σ}(ρ) is defined dually by α_0 = 1, i.e. U = a. Now the determinant condition forces δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b). So this is only a partial section, over the subgroup τ'_{ρ,σ} = {(a,b) ∈ T_ρ × N'_σ : δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b)}. This subgroup is Ker(ε_3: τ_{ρ,σ} → μ_n) = T_ρ ×_{μ_n} N'_σ (formula (47)).

On the next page, in the modular case, he renames these M(1/2) = M(σ) and M(-j) = M(ρ). He then transports them by conjugation with ρ to get a family M(q) indexed by the anharmonic orbit of special points on the λ-line, using q ↦ 1/(1-q), which has order 3. So these are local 'decomposition-type' subgroups attached to the elliptic points of the modular curve (j = 1728 ↔ λ ∈ {-1, 1/2, 2}; j = 0 ↔ λ = -j, -j²). The purpose is to encode how the arithmetic (Galois/GT) action interacts with the order-2 and order-3 torsion, i.e. the orbifold points of M_{1,1}.
errors: Equation number (43) is reused: it was already used on p.540 for the determinant condition. This is a bookkeeping slip only.
In (45) the triple is written '∈ M_{ρ,σ}' while (44) has '∈ Γ M_{ρ,σ}'. This is a notational inconsistency, presumably harmless.

The verification is consistent with the p.540 proposition. With U=b the determinant constraint reduces to the defining condition of τ_{ρ,σ}, so this is a full section. With U=a it forces δ_ρ(a)=δ_σ(b), so only a partial section over τ'. Implicitly u must also be chosen (det u = μ); this is not addressed on this page.

ideas.what: Defining distinguished subgroups ('sub-group-relations') of the relation group M_{ρ,σ} by fixing the G-component to equal the σ-component (resp. the ρ-component). These give a section over τ_{ρ,σ} and a partial section over the kernel τ'_{ρ,σ} = T_ρ ×_{μ_n} N'_σ.
ideas.modern_name: splittings/sections of an extension; fibre product over the cyclotomic quotient μ_n

ideas.what: Attaching local subgroups to the elliptic (orbifold) points of the modular curve (order 2 ↔ λ=1/2,-1,2; order 3 ↔ λ=-j,-j²). These are permuted by the order-3 homography q ↦ 1/(1-q) acting on the six special points, as a tool in the loop equation for the GT-type group.
ideas.modern_name: action of GT / Galois on torsion elements and orbifold (elliptic) points of the mapping class group / M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (late 1990s); B. Collas (2010s, GT action on torsion of mapping class groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme stresses the role of the 'points à automorphismes' of modular multiplicities in the Teichmüller tower, but without these constructions

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically indexes subgroup-relations by the anharmonic set of special points on the λ-line (including the elliptic points 1/2, -1, 2, -j). This builds the orbifold (torsion) points of M_{1,1} directly into the definition of the group of relations for the loop equation. It anticipates later work on GT actions on torsion/orbifold points (Collas, Nakamura), but in a different formalism via sections over τ_{ρ,σ} and τ'_{ρ,σ}.
missed.quote: On définit du même M_{ρ,σ}(ρ) par α_0 = 1 i.e. α = f ... ce qui fait une section partielle au-dessus de τ'_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The work could offer an alternative presentation of GT-type groups incorporating elliptic-point data. That may be relevant to versions of GT built from orbifold/torsion relations. The idea is only sketched here and unfinished (cf. 'Il resterait...' on the next page).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly routine bookkeeping: defining sections of an extension. The interesting part is its place in a program attaching subgroups to the elliptic points of the modular curve within the loop equation. That points to an unpublished orbifold-point approach to GT, but it is not developed on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'i.e. (cf [?] π̂_0 [?])' should read 'i.e. (cf (40))': β = f iff U = b follows from formula (40).
'forme une section [?]' reads more like 'fournit une section'.

'de façon la plus simple de la relever en un élément ... suivant il par par [?] (a,b,U b = b)!' is probably 'la façon la plus simple de le relever en un élément (a,b,U) de M_{ρ,σ} n'est-il pas (a,b,U=b)!'.
'(Et on a aussi δ_a(U) = δ_σ(b))' should be read as δ_G(U) = δ_σ(b).
'ce qui fait une section partielle [-...-] dessus de τ'' reads 'ce qui fait une section partielle au-dessus de τ'_{ρ,σ}'.
'On définit du même' is likely 'On définit de même'.
